memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'"The priest shall then put on his linen clothes, with linen undergarments next to his body, and shall remove the ashes of the burnt offering that the fire has consumed on the altar and place them beside the altar."'" - Lev 6:10 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The high and holy priest of Israel begins his day by shovelling ashes.

Dressed in his sacred linen, he clears out yesterday's remains. It is menial, dirty, repetitive work — and God specifically commanded it as part of the priestly office.

There is dignity here for everyone doing unglamorous work.

We tend to divide labour into the significant and the mundane. Preaching is spiritual; cleaning is not. Leading is important; maintaining is not. But God wrote ash-removal into the job description of the holiest office in Israel, and He required it be done in holy garments.

The ashes mattered because of what they were: the evidence that a sacrifice had been accepted. Handling them was handling the proof of God's mercy.

Jesus, who knew exactly who He was, took a towel and washed feet (Jn 13:3-5). Paul told slaves — people doing the least regarded work in the empire — that whatever you do, work at it with all your heart, as working for the Lord (Col 3:23).

If today's work is dishes, spreadsheets, nappies, or invoices, you are not doing something less spiritual than the person on the platform. God put ashes in a priest's hands.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I rank my activities into "spiritual" and "ordinary"?
2. What unglamorous task could I do today as genuine service to God?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You gave the priest ashes to carry and You washed Your disciples' feet. Teach me to find You in the ordinary work of today. Amen.
